gaps.sentence: ___ everyone in the office passed the safety test.
gaps.hint: the only adverb that can modify 'everyone'
gaps.explanation: 'Almost everyone' is the standard pattern; 'each', 'all' and 'every' cannot directly precede 'everyone'.

gaps.sentence: Don't worry, we still have ___ time before the gates close.
gaps.hint: positive meaning: there is some time; 'time' is uncountable
gaps.explanation: 'A little time' means some time, which reassures; 'time' is uncountable.

gaps.sentence: He took ___ notice of the warning and carried on as before.
gaps.explanation: 'Take little notice of' means to pay hardly any attention; 'notice' is uncountable here.

gaps.sentence: ___ of the students has been given a personal timetable.
gaps.hint: this is the only option that can be followed by 'of' and take a singular verb
gaps.explanation: 'Each of the students has ...' is correct; 'every' cannot take 'of' here and 'all/both' need a plural verb.

gaps.sentence: There were ___ interruptions this year, so the ceremony ran far more smoothly.
___ the information you gave was correct.
gaps.explanation: 'All the information' is correct; 'none/neither' would need 'of' and 'both' requires two separate countable items.

gaps.sentence: ___ of my friends knew about the concert, so I went on my own.
gaps.explanation: 'None of my friends' means zero friends; 'no' cannot stand before 'of' and 'nothing' is not a quantifier here.

gaps.sentence: There are plenty ___ chairs for everyone.
gaps.hint: 'plenty' is always followed by this preposition before a noun
gaps.explanation: 'Plenty of + noun' is the fixed pattern; no other preposition follows 'plenty'.
